categories.main_business_segments: Highwoods Properties, Inc. operates primarily as a fully integrated office real estate investment trust (REIT). Its main business segments are the ownership, development, acquisition, leasing, and management of office properties, primarily located in the best business districts (BBDs) of Atlanta, Charlotte, Nashville, Orlando, Pittsburgh, Raleigh, Richmond, and Tampa. The company also engages in selective mixed-use and land development activities, but its core focus is on high-quality office buildings.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Highwoods utilizes a fully integrated operational model, managing leasing, property management, maintenance, and customer service in-house rather than outsourcing. The company emphasizes proactive preventative maintenance, build-to-suit construction, and space modification, including tenant improvements and expansions. It leverages technology for property management, information security, and sustainability initiatives, including energy efficiency and environmental impact reduction.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The company serves a diverse base of office tenants, including large corporations, government agencies, financial institutions, law firms, healthcare, insurance, and technology companies. Its largest customers include the Federal Government, Bank of America, Asurion, MetLife, Bridgestone, and others, with no single tenant accounting for more than 4% of annualized cash rental revenue. The primary end market is high-quality office space in urban and suburban business districts.
categories.geographic_coverage: Highwoods' operations are concentrated in the Southeastern and Mid-Atlantic United States, with core markets in Atlanta, Charlotte, Nashville, Orlando, Pittsburgh, Raleigh, Richmond, and Tampa. The company maintains division offices in each of these cities and does not rely heavily on any single geographic market for its revenues.
categories.supply_chain_position: Highwoods operates as an owner, developer, and operator of office properties, positioning it downstream in the real estate supply chain. It is responsible for delivering finished, managed office space to end users (tenants), and does not engage in construction contracting or raw material supply.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s strategic focus is on placemaking—creating high-quality, amenitized workplaces in dynamic business districts to help tenants attract and retain talent. Highwoods emphasizes continuous portfolio upgrading through acquisitions, developments, and recycling of non-core assets. It is committed to ESG initiatives, including sustainability, energy efficiency, and diversity, and maintains a conservative, flexible balance sheet to support opportunistic growth.
categories.revenue_model: Highwoods generates revenue primarily through rental income from office properties, including base rent and cost recovery income (such as CAM, property taxes, and insurance). Additional revenue streams include parking income, lease termination fees, and development/construction management fees from joint ventures. The company also realizes gains from property dispositions as part of its capital recycling strategy.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Highwoods competes with other office REITs, financial institutions, pension funds, partnerships, and private investors in its markets. Key competitors include both domestic and foreign REITs and large institutional investors. The company positions itself as a leading provider of high-quality, differentiated office space in vibrant business districts, leveraging its fully integrated model and local market expertise.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of December 31, 2021, Highwoods owned 27.4 million square feet of office space with a market capitalization of approximately $4.8 billion. In 2021, rental and other revenues were $768 million, with net income of $323 million and funds from operations (FFO) of $416 million. The company has demonstrated growth through acquisitions and development, with a recent focus on upgrading its portfolio and entering higher-growth markets like Charlotte.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Highwoods differentiates itself by focusing on high-quality, amenitized office environments in the most dynamic business districts, offering in-house management and customer service for greater responsiveness and cost efficiency. Its placemaking strategy aims to create workplaces that help tenants attract and retain top talent. The company’s integrated approach, strong balance sheet, and commitment to ESG and sustainability further enhance its value proposition to tenants and investors.
